title: Pausanias, Description of Greece 1.31.2: the route of the Hyperborean first-fruits to Delos
language: Greek (Spiro 1903) / English (W. H. S. Jones and H. A. Ormerod 1918-1935)
source: Paris gr. 1410 via Gallica (BnF) + Spiro's Greek (Perseus) + Jones's English (Loeb, Perseus)
description: Pausanias on the first-fruits of the Hyperboreans, passed by the Arimaspi, Issedones and Scythians to Sinope and through Greece to Prasiae in Attica, and taken by the Athenians to Delos (1.31.2), on Paris gr. 1410.
introduction:
Describing the Attic deme of Prasiae, Pausanias reports that the first-fruits of the Hyperboreans are sent there: the Hyperboreans hand them to the Arimaspi, these to the Issedones, the Scythians bring them to Sinope, Greeks carry them on to Prasiae, and the Athenians take them to Delos, hidden in wheat straw. Herodotus (4.33) and Callimachus (Hymn 4) give other routes.

All manuscripts of Pausanias are late, of the 15th century. The one shown is Paris, BnF, grec 1410, copied in 1491 by Michael Souliardos (siglum Pa); the older Venice manuscript (Marc. gr. 413) has no published images. The BnF's images are made from microfilm, each showing an opening of two pages, cropped here to the page; each page has 30 lines. 1.31.2 stands at the foot of fol. 26v (the folio number is taken from the neighbouring openings: the next opening's recto reads 28).
translator_notes: Greek: Spiro's Teubner text via Perseus, not a transcription of the manuscript.
English: Jones's Loeb translation via Perseus; Jones's footnotes are omitted.

translation.original_text: ἐν δὲ Πρασιεῦσιν Ἀπόλλωνός ἐστι ναός· ἐνταῦθα τὰς Ὑπερβορέων ἀπαρχὰς ἰέναι λέγεται, παραδιδόναι δὲ αὐτὰς Ὑπερβορέους μὲν Ἀριμασποῖς, Ἀριμασποὺς δʼ Ἰσσηδόσι, παρὰ δὲ τούτων Σκύθας ἐς Σινώπην κομίζειν, ἐντεῦθεν δὲ φέρεσθαι διὰ Ἑλλήνων ἐς Πρασιάς, Ἀθηναίους δὲ εἶναι τοὺς ἐς Δῆλον ἄγοντας· τὰς δὲ ἀπαρχὰς κεκρύφθαι μὲν ἐν καλάμῃ πυρῶν, γινώσκεσθαι δὲ ὑπʼ οὐδένων. ἔστι δὲ μνῆμα ἐπὶ Πρασιαῖς Ἐρυσίχθονος, ὡς ἐκομίζετο ὀπίσω μετὰ τὴν θεωρίαν ἐκ Δήλου, γενομένης οἱ κατὰ τὸν πλοῦν τῆς τελευτῆς.
translation.text: At Prasiae is a temple of Apollo. Hither they say are sent the first-fruits of the Hyperboreans, and the Hyperboreans are said to hand them over to the Arimaspi, the Arimaspi to the Issedones, from these the Scythians bring them to Sinope, thence they are carried by Greeks to Prasiae, and the Athenians take them to Delos. The first-fruits are hidden in wheat straw, and they are known of none. There is at Prasiae a monument to Erysichthon, who died on the voyage home from Delos, after the sacred mission thither.
translation.scan_note: 1.31.2 begins in fol. 26v line 23, ‹ἐν δὲ πρασιεῦσιν ἀπόλλωνός ἐστι ναός›, and ends with the last line of the page (30); the facing fol. 27r begins with 1.31.3, ‹κραναὸν δὲ τὸν βασιλεύσαντα ἀθηναίων›. Lines 21-30 were checked by eye; the count from the top of the page is by line detection. Read on the BnF image (image 34).
